Hello, I’m Dr. Martínez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m glad you’re here. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—the EPDS—to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; there are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays confidential within our care team. My goal is to understand how you’re doing so we can best support you.

Let’s start gently:

1. Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt hard to do?

I’ve still been able to laugh sometimes—like when my little guy makes those silly faces while he’s sleeping—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Most of the time I catch myself smiling, but it feels kind of forced, like I have to remind myself to enjoy the moment instead of it just happening naturally.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes, yes… I can laugh, especially when my baby gives those big milk-drunk grins, but it feels kind of distant, like I’m working harder to feel it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few small things—like taking the baby out in the stroller for a short walk or having my morning coffee—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it was before she was born. Mostly I just think, “I hope I have the energy to get through it,” rather than really anticipating it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday she was fussy for hours and I kept thinking, “Maybe I’m not feeding her right,” or “I should know what she needs.” I know, rationally, babies cry, but I still catch myself wondering if I’m just not doing a good-enough job.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll be sitting on the couch, everything quiet, and suddenly my chest feels tight because I’m sure something’s wrong—maybe her breathing changed, or I think I forgot to fasten the diaper right. After a minute I can talk myself down, but it pops up out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had any full-blown panic attacks, but there’ve been moments—usually at night—when my heart starts racing and I feel this wave of dread, like something bad is about to happen even though everything looks fine. It passes pretty quickly if I get up and walk around or check on the baby, but it’s unsettling while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… some days it feels like the pile of tiny chores—laundry, bottles, making sure I eat—just stacks up faster than I can handle it. I usually manage to push through, but I end those hours feeling kind of frazzled, like I’m one dropped pacifier away from losing track of everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve been unhappy off and on, but once I finally lie down I still drift off pretty quickly—maybe because I’m so tired from the day. I do sometimes toss and turn for a bit if I start replaying everything I think I did wrong, but it hasn’t turned into full-blown insomnia.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—like a heavy, blah cloud that lingers even when everything looks fine on the outside. It’s not every minute, but it shows up a couple of days a week and makes everything feel sort of gray and flat.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A little—maybe once or twice this week. One night she wouldn’t settle and I just sat in the rocker with tears rolling down while I bounced her. It wasn’t sobbing, more like quiet crying that stopped once she finally fell asleep.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed and tired, but I haven’t had any thoughts of hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit

**Presenting emotional / behavioral symptoms**  
- Low mood (“sad, heavy, blah cloud” several days/week) with brief crying episode  
- Marked reduction in pleasure/enjoyment relative to baseline  
- Excessive self-blame and guilt (“not doing a good-enough job”)  
- Unprovoked anxiety (tight chest, racing heart, dread) multiple times daily; no panic attacks per se  
- Feeling overwhelmed by routine infant care tasks  

**Observed patterns**  
- Symptoms present ≥5 days/week, interfering with emotional engagement and coping  
- Sleep onset preserved; some pre-sleep rumination  
- No suicidal or self-harm ideation endorsed  

**Screening relevance**  
Meets sub-threshold to mild range for perinatal depression/anxiety (PHQ-9 items 2, 3, 8, 9; GAD-7 items 4, 6).  
No acute safety concerns. Recommend formal assessment with standardized perinatal depression/anxiety scale and follow-up monitoring.
